title: Grateful Dead Live at Monterey Fairgrounds on 1967-06-18
source: Lineage:  SBD Master Reels > DAT (Panasonic 3700) > Delta DiO 2496 > PC hard drive > CDR > CDWAV > Cool Edit > Traders Little Helper

ai_review.summary: Clean soundboard capture of the historic Monterey Pop set with solid jamming on Viola Lee Blues, though the performance is viewed as more a historical curiosity than a standout show.
ai_review.review: The recording offers an unusually clear and well‑balanced sound for this early festival appearance, making it a valuable document of the Dead’s June 18 1967 Monterey Pop slot. While the set isn’t hailed as a classic—listeners describe it as decent jamming with the highlight being Viola Lee Blues—the historical significance and the surprisingly clean audio keep it worthwhile.

ai_rating.rationale: Recording quality is praised as clean and superior to other sources, but reviewers are split on the musical impact, calling it a solid historical document rather than an exceptional performance.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very nice and clean; listeners note it sounds better than other available versions with no major drop‑outs or muffiness mentioned.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Short festival slot featuring early blues/folk material; the set feels more like a historical snapshot than a tightly crafted concert.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Reviewer notes Jerry’s playing on Viola Lee Blues, likening his stage pose to George Harrison's.
